message.reasoning_content:
The image shows a TAG Heuer Link Calibre 5 Automatic with black dial, stainless steel case and the distinctive Link bracelet. Reference number: WBC2110.BA0603 is the Link Calibre 5 41mm black dial on steel bracelet. Let me think.

TAG Heuer Link Calibre 5 Automatic 41mm — reference WBC2110.BA0603. Yes, that's commonly cited. The "BC" series is Link. W = three-hand, B = ?, C = Link series... Actually per the rules: position 1 `W` three-hand, positions 2-3 series (`BC` Link), position 4 movement (1 quartz, 2 automatic...). Hmm, WBC doesn't have a digit at position 4. Actually the format is W + 2 letters + digit? "WBP201A" — W, BP (Aquaracer), 2 (automatic), 0 (size class), 1 (metal), A (dial). So WBC2110: W, BC (Link), 2 (automatic), 1 (size), 1 (metal steel), 0 (dial version). Then strap code BA0603.

So reference WBC2110.BA0603. Black dial — hmm, dial version digit 0. There's also WBC2112 (blue) and WBC2111? Let me recall. TAG Heuer Link Calibre 5: WBC2110.BA0603 black dial 41mm; WBC2111.BA0603? Actually the blue one is WBC2112.BA0603. The black is WBC2110.BA0603. I'll go with that.

Movement: automatic. Case material: stainless-steel. Bracelet: metal. Confidence ~0.7.

Note there's also the date window at 3 — yes the Calibre 5 Link has date at 3. Good.

Also WBC2110 has the 41mm; there is also 43mm? Link Calibre 5 came in 41mm. Fine.

Bracelet code BA0603 is the Link bracelet. Some references list WBC2110.BA0603.

Confidence 0.65.
